identifier: COLREG 1972; adopted 20 October 1972; entry into force 15 July 1977
notes: Risk-of-collision context of the CPA/TCPA detector. Rule 7: proper use of radar including long-range scanning and radar plotting or equivalent systematic observation of detected objects; no assumptions on scanty (radar) information; 7(d)(i): 'such risk shall be deemed to exist if the compass bearing of an approaching vessel does not appreciably change' (7(d)(ii): risk may exist even with an appreciable bearing change, e.g. very large vessels, tows, close range). Rule 8(d): avoiding action shall result in passing at a safe distance. COLREGs give no numeric CPA/TCPA limits. Dates from the IMO convention page; Rule 7(d)(i) wording confirmed in several reproductions; the wording of Rule 7(b) and 8(d) was seen only in secondary copies (check the official text before quoting).

title: Revised Guidelines for the Onboard Operational Use of Shipborne Automatic Identification Systems (AIS)
identifier: Resolution A.1106(29), adopted 2 December 2015; revokes A.917(22) as amended by A.956(23)

title: Analysis of Collision Threat Parameters and Criteria
identifier: The Journal of Navigation 68(5): 887-896; doi:10.1017/S0373463315000223

issuerOrAuthors: Holtrop, J.; Mennen, G. G. J. (MARIN)
identifier: International Shipbuilding Progress 29 (No. 335 per common citation), pp. 166-170, July 1982; DOI not confirmed

title: Speed loss due to added resistance in wind and waves
identifier: The Naval Architect (RINA), 2008, pp. 14-16 (month not confirmed)
notes: The speed-loss method implemented by the legacy (simplified Townsin-Kwon): dV/V1 x 100 % = C_beta C_U C_Form, V2 = V1 (1 - dV/V1); BN as sea-state input; direction from the bow (0 deg = head sea). Confirmed through secondary reproductions: head sea C_beta = 1 (0-30 deg), bow sea 2 C_beta = 1.7 - 0.03 (BN-4)^2 (30-60 deg), container-ship normal-loading C_Form with divisor 22.0. Not verified: beam 0.9 - 0.06 (BN-6)^2, following 0.4 - 0.03 (BN-8)^2 and the C_U polynomials (they match the legacy code, which is not verification). Legacy deviations: C_Form variant, banded C_B, inverted use (V1 from observed V2). Full text not read.

title: Approximate formulae for the speed loss due to added resistance in wind and waves
issuerOrAuthors: Townsin, R. L.; Kwon, Y. J.
identifier: Transactions of the Royal Institution of Naval Architects 125 (July 1983), pp. 199-207 (TRID 417181); some sources write 1982
notes: Approximate formulae for the percentage speed loss in head weather by Beaufort number for container ships and tankers, laden and in ballast; bow, beam and following weather as fractions of the head-weather loss. Ship form coefficient C_Form = 0.5 BN + BN^6.5/(2.7 V^(2/3)) (laden) or 0.7 BN + BN^6.5/(2.7 V^(2/3)) (ballast), V = displacement volume in m3 (from an earlier ScienceDirect Topics excerpt). The legacy (0.7 BN + BN^6.5)/(2.2 Delta^(2/3)) matches no published variant. Correction applied: volume, pages and TRID URL.

title: State-of-the-art technologies, measures, and potential for reducing GHG emissions from shipping - A review
issuerOrAuthors: Bouman, E. A.; Lindstad, E.; Rialland, A. I.; Stromman, A. H.
identifier: Transportation Research Part D: Transport and Environment 52: 408-421; doi:10.1016/j.trd.2017.03.022
notes: Review of about 150 studies: per-measure CO2-reduction ranges against a baseline ship; no single measure suffices; more than 75 % reduction by 2050 possible with combined measures. Ranges taken from a secondary reproduction of its table (check against the paper): air lubrication 1-15 %, hull coating 1-10 %, waste heat recovery 1-20 %, wind 1-50 %, solar 0.2-12 %, fuel cells 2-20 %, cold ironing 3-10 %; propulsion efficiency devices 1-25 % (ITF citing Bouman). Legacy values: air lubrication 8 % inside; hull coating 10 % = maximum; WHR 10 % inside; PED 13 % = midpoint; solar 12 % and fuel cells 20 % = maximum; wind 15 % inside. No ranges found for resistance-reduction devices, power system/machinery, LNG or biofuel. The ranges are ship-level CO2 reductions: not fractions of auxiliary-engine fuel and not to be scaled by time at sea. Correction applied: verified bibliography and ranges.

title: Identifying Global Patterns of Transshipment Behavior
issuerOrAuthors: Miller, N. A.; Roan, A.; Hochberg, T.; Amos, J.; Kroodsma, D. A.
identifier: Frontiers in Marine Science 5: 240 (published 23 July 2018); doi:10.3389/fmars.2018.00240
license: Open access (Frontiers, CC BY; not re-checked)
notes: GFW encounter: two vessels within 500 m for at least 2 h at median speed < 2 kn, at least 10 km from a coastal anchorage (sensitivity analysis 1/2/4/6 kn, 2/6/10/12 h, 250/500/1,000 m); loitering: a transshipment vessel < 2 kn for at least 8 h at least 20 nm from shore. The legacy detector differs (speed difference 0.5/2/10 kn, distance 27/34/600 m, heading score, 30-min windows, score >= 70). Citable baseline for calibrating the v2 transhipment detector. Encounter rule confirmed via the GFW definition, not verbatim from the Methods.

issuerOrAuthors: Welch, H.; Clavelle, T.; White, T. D.; et al.
identifier: Science Advances 8(44): eabq2109 (2 November 2022); doi:10.1126/sciadv.abq2109

Far longer than the v2 30-min rule, which needs its own justification. Code: https://github.com/GlobalFishingWatch/AIS-disabling-high-seas. issuerOrAuthors: Natale, F.; Gibin, M.; Alessandrini, A.; Vespe, M.; Paulrud, A.

issuerOrAuthors: de Souza, E. N.; Boerder, K.; Matwin, S.; Worm, B.
identifier: PLOS ONE 11(7): e0158248; doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0158248 (correction notice PLOS ONE 11(9): e0163760)
